notes.title: Grid Creeps Patch 5
notes.notes:
Hey there, I wasn't expecting to release a patch this soon after the last one, but the difference this change makes is worth a Patch all its own. The AI has been fixed and optimized, improving the middle/late Game experience.

The late Game had an imperfection in the AI logic that is hard to explain; the simple answer is that to find its way the AI switches between methods of pathfinding but would get stuck on one of them. It would have trouble finding its way after running into a barrier. When there were a bunch of Creeps, turrets firing and things were crazy it wasn't easy to see- some Creeps might never have found their way to the HQ if left unchecked though.

As the Game progresses there are more Creeps per Wave, so more Creeps finding their way around the mountains. This would slow the Game down as you progressed up in Levels, making the mid-late Game slow during attacks- even on good computers. This got worse the farther you got in the Game. This has been massively improved, the Game performs significantly better. 

On an unrelated note, I took a Job that will last the rest of this Week and part of next so I won't get as much done in that time. Game Design doesn't pay the Bills yet, but I'm hoping that will change sometime in the next Year or two. I will still be working on the Game- just not as much until this Job is finished. Fear not! I work for myself remodeling so I make my own hours and I'm not going anywhere. If anything, these jobs motivate me more, I want to get out of remodeling permanently and focus %100 of my time on Game Design. I thought you may want to know why I won't be around as much in the immediate future but that's enough about me.

And that's it for this one. There's no official changelog other than to say the AI has been drastically improved. I hope this improves your enjoyment of the Game! Toodle-oo!

notes.title: Grid Creeps Patch 4
notes.notes:
Hey folks, there's a new Patch out! The Holidays slowed me down, but I'm back to getting things done.

The Patch adds 23 Achievements. You will find a list of them below. If you have any Saves you can get some of the Achievements by Loading one of  them, but you won't be able to get all of them this way, you will need to start a New Game to get the rest.

The Upgrade 'All' Button used to only appear when selecting a Wall. It is now working for everything that you can Upgrade. I have been wanting to add this for a while, it was time consuming, but it's one more feature I can check off the list. Hopefully this will save you some time when you're building many Towers at once.

I've added 5 stats on the Main Menu- Red, Green, Blue and Yellow Creep Kills along with  Total Kills. From here on out you'll be able to keep track of your Kills.  In the future there will be a dedicated Section that tracks this and many more statistics, the Main Menu is a temporary spot for showing this. It was tracking these stats for the Achievements anyway so I thought I may as well display them somewhere, and since there is one of each Creep on the Main Menu, I'd put it next to them until I get the other Stats added- you'll see them when you boot up the Game.

Expect a progress report soon to let you know what is going on moving forward. If anyone has any feedback, please let me know! 

[h3]Achievements[/h3]

1 Novice: Kill 50 Creeps

2 Good: Kill 500 Creeps

3 Epic: Kill 1,000 Creeps

4 Master: Kill 5,000 Creeps

5 King: Kill 10,000 Creeps

6 Red Slayer: Kill 1,000 Red Creeps

7 Green Slayer: Kill 1,000 Green Creeps

8 Blue Slayer: Kill 2,500 Blue or Mini Creeps

9 Yellow Slayer: Kill 1,000 Yellow Creeps

10 Carpenter: Build All Wood Based Towers in the same Game (Archer, Fire Archer, Crossbow, Ballista)

11 Iron Smith: Build All Iron Based Towers in the same Game (Sentry Gun, Shotgun, Mgun, Sniper)

12 Steel Smith: Build All Steel Based Towers in the same Game (Cannon, Artillery, Rocket, Missile)

13 Engineer: Build All Power Based Towers in the same Game (Blaster, Lightning, Laser, Rail Gun)

14 Tower Master: Build All Towers in the same Game (16 Total)

15 Builder: Build at least one of each Building/Mine

16 Outpost: Survive to Wave 5

17 Village: Survive to Wave 10

18 Town: Survive to Wave 25

19 City: Survive to Wave 50

20 Metropolis: Survive to Wave 75

21 Capital: Survive to Wave 100

22 Wood Challenge: Survive to Wave 30 using only Wood Based Towers

23 Iron Challenge: Survive to Wave 30 using only Iron Based Towers

notes.title: Progress Report 5
notes.notes:
Hey folks, I thought I should give an update. Happy-New-Decade! I got a bit distracted by the Holidays and took a few Days off- it had been a while, I've been at this for a long time and not taken a proper break since before initial Release. 

The Achievements are taking a little bit longer than expected as well. The implementation is pretty easy but the Art is taking longer than I thought they would. There are going to be 23 Achievements as of this Progress Report. It's kind of funny, I thought it would be the other way around- that the Art would be easy but the code side be tricky, but that's life I guess. The Achievements Patch is coming in the next few Days.

In making the Achievements I got to thinking about Stat tracking. It might be neat to know how many Creeps you've killed throughout all your Games, or how many of each Tower/Building you've built in all. There could potentially be a lot of these. I am not sure they will make it into the next Patch, which adds Achievements, but adding most of the ideas I have should not take too long.

There is also a new Trailer, which was released a few Days ago. I played a lot of the Game in that time, built a few nice bases. It had been a while since I got as far as I did on the last Base built for the Trailer. It got me thinking more about the late Game and how some of the Upgrades scale. I may be doing some small adjustments in the future, aimed at the late Game, though I haven't decided exactly what to adjust yet so I can't say much more than this right now. Sometimes deciding what to do takes longer than actually doing it and this is one of those cases- decisions, decisions! 

I am also going to be re-visiting the AI soon. This is something I've been looking forward to improving for a while- it's the type of challenge that I enjoy a lot. The late Game can get Laggy, even on good computers. This is largely due to how the AI works. I am fairly certain I know how to greatly improve performance and there has always been a minor imperfection in how it decides what path finding method to use. The Enemies are suppose to toggle between a few different methods of findingtheir way depending on circumstances but it can get stuck on one of them. I didn't catch this at first and it may not even be apparent if you don't know how it is intended to behave. This is another late Game issue that I was reminded of while playing. One thing at a time though, that's the only way to make it through a project this big.

Thank you all for your support! I wish I could get these Patches out faster- it gets a bit overwhelming sometimes but the majority of the Project is finished and these last few things are steadily getting checked off. 

I think that's it for this one. Expect a Patch in the next few Days. I hope your Holidays went well, take care folks!

notes.title: Grid Creeps Patch 3
notes.notes:
Time for Update number 3! Happy Holidays!

While the changelog is not long, there is one big feature that has been added with this Update- the High Score system. When selecting which map you want to play on you can see the Highest Wave you've gotten to for each Difficulty. You will need to start new Games in order for it to record your scores though, Save Games from before this update won't count, though you can still play them. 
*For clarification- this is only pre-Patch Saves, you can Save/Load Post-Patch Saves and they'll still count toward the High Score as they should.

The Steam API is also now working with the Game. You should be able to use Steam normally while in Game. This is the first step to adding achievements which I hope to get working with the next Update.

Achievements and the new Tutorial are the big Goals for the next Update. the Tutorial has been halfway done since last update; It took most of the Week to get the High Score system finished so I didn't get to work on it at all. You can also expect more Overall improvements to the Game with the next Update.

The next Update will probably be about 2 Weeks from this post, though I'll post a Progress Report sometime next Week to let you all know what's going on.

Hope your Holidays are going well, and Happy Early New-Year!




[h3]v.0.6.43 Changelog[/h3]


-High Score system added. This shows the Highest Wave you have gotten to for each Level/Difficulty. The High Score updates on Game Over. Sandbox Mode does not keep track of High Scores.
	*Saves from before this patch aren't compatible with the system. While you can continue to play old Saves, they won't count towards a High Score.

-Steam API has been added- you should be able to use Steam and its features while in Game now. This is also the first step to linking Achievements.

-Fixed crash when selecting Crossbow after converting from the Archer.

-Coal Mine was labeled Coal Cutter... it is properly labeled now.
        EDIT: It is still labeled Coal Cutter. I guess I didn't fix that after all. So ya, it's fixed now but I don't think a Patch just for this is worth it, so next patch it will be fixed.

notes.title: Grid Creeps Patch 2
notes.notes:
Hello again Folks, It’s time for another Patch! I have been very busy improving the Game over the last couple Weeks.  I have still been primarily addressing feedback and trying to get the HUD to a more finalized state and it has been some work! Quite a bit more than I thought actually- partly because I made more changes that I was originally planning, but also because HUD work is time consuming.

Seeing other people play and the feedback I got highlighted how the HUD had some problems and information in some places was vague, hard to read, in need of a background, or in some cases misleading; I saw how, in being the developer, there are things that are obvious to me (because I made the Game), but aren’t obvious to other people. I thought a lot about how I could make important information more plain to see and straight-forward to access, how I could make the game more intuitive and easier to play and I made the changes that needed to be made. That thinking eats up a lot of time which I still forget to take into account! The Game should just plain be easier to play.

There are still some smaller things I want to improve about the HUD, but I believe that this may be the first 1.0-worthy version of it. I was hoping to get the High Score system in this update but I really wanted to nail down the HUD. I am hoping that the next patch will be about 1 Week from the release of this patch, give or take a day or two. I’m about half-way done with both the High Score system and the new Tutorial. I hope to get both of these out by then, but things never go %100 according to plan. Or maybe things go faster than expected, an earlier than expected release would be nice. In any case, there's still a lot to do, expect updates regularly for the next few months. 

Anyway, I've added 4 new screenshots. I hope that this newest version is to your liking! Thank you all for your help, your opinions are Gold to this project. Please tell me what kind of changes you think could make this game better! Take care everyone!


[h3]v.0.05.42 Changelog- [/h3]

-After 3 upgrades (Level 4) you can convert your Tower into something better. The Archer can convert into a Fire Archer, Crossbow or Ballista – the Sentry Gun can convert into a Shotgun, Machine Gun or Sniper. The Cannon and Blaster have their own conversions as well. It was not made clear to the player that this mechanic has been in the Game since the beginning. Before, the buttons to convert into these Towers were hidden until you had upgraded the Tower to Level 4. Now, they are visible any time you select the Tower- if your Tower is at Level 1-3  the unusable version of the button is visible and if you mouse over the button it will give you information about the Tower and it tells you in clear Yellow text that you need to Upgrade to Level 4 before you can convert the Tower. The buttons always being there for the player to investigate and the information you get from trying to use them should make this mechanic much more obvious. 

-HUD has seen many more improvements. Smaller tweaks may not be listed. 

-All In-Game text now has backgrounds which should make all of the text much easier to read.

-New Font: Dosis- the old letters were all the same width, for example- an 'i' took up just as much space as a 'W', which gave an odd look to certain words depending on their spelling and made words longer than they need to be. The new Font varies in width, so an 'i' takes up less space than the 'W'. Words are a bit shorter and some text required some editing. *I may not have caught everything yet; Some text may not be perfectly placed but this should be rare. The new Font also fits more in with the vision I have of the Final Product, I hope you like the new look better!
	-This allowed me to shrink parts of the HUD further.
	**Font has only been changed for the HUD/Gameplay, Out of Game Menus still use the old Font- this will be updated to match at some point as well.

-When hovering over one of the Buy buttons text would appear above it with information about cost and a description. When you couldn't afford something it would tell you what you needed, but it was hard to read and was easy to miss/ignore. This information has all been moved to the right side of the screen, a background has been added and descriptions revised. When buying something it should be much more clear what you are getting. And when you can't afford something it is easier to tell why- it highlights what you are short on in red if you don't have what you need to build something.
	*Houses and Walls also said they required Population, they don't and never actually did- the description was wrong. This has been fixed.

-The buttons on the left side of the screen have been changed. Before there were 5 permanent Menu/Options/etc. buttons that were always there. Now there is just one button that accesses the others. when selected the others appear and you can exit the game or return to the menu. 'Escape' also toggles these Buttons and like everything else, right click can cancel these Menus/buttons.

-Food, Population, Warehouse Limit information has been made a little bit smaller. These and the Resource Bars that are under them have been moved to the right, giving the player yet more screen space.

-The background behind 'Wave:#' in the top middle has been made even smaller to account for the new Font.

-When starting or loading a Game, you would need to hit the space bar twice to Pause, though clicking the Pause button has always worked properly. Now you don’t have to double tap the space bar the first time to Pause the Game.

-When anything you have built is selected the information that pops up in the upper right corner of the screen has been made smaller, giving *drumroll*… more screen-space!

-If you want to upgrade a selected Tower or Mine and cannot you are either short on Gold, Resources or Population. It always told you how much of each is required, but gave no clear signs what you were short on; now it highlights what you are short on in Red.

-When placing your Headquarters the round Preview marker now changes colors depending on what resources are in range of the HQ, this should help Players find a Good spot to place the HQ. This isn’t listed anywhere in-game yet (just one little thing I haven’t gotten to yet): Red = no Gold or Wood in range, Yellow = only Wood or only Gold in range but the other is not, Grey = Wood and Gold are in Range but Iron is not, Dark Green = Gold, Wood and Iron are in range but Coal is not, Bright Green = All Resources are in range. Grey or either of the Greens are likely good starting spots.

-The Laser used to go through Mountains/Terrain Obstructions. Lasers are stopped by them now.

-Many Tower/Building/Mine descriptions have been edited/revised, giving more useful information and explaining things more clearly.

-Main Buy Buttons along the bottom have been shaded to match the Button's border. This makes it a little bit easier to tell the different groups apart. Hopefully you will agree that it also just plain look better.

-If you right clicked while hovering over a Tower Conversion button or Target Priority you would no longer be able to select any of what you have built (though buttons were still usable). It was caused by a simple code order issue. This has been fixed.

-In the beginning of the Tutorial it tells you the menu is the Save button- shrinking the HUD moved the side buttons up but i missed moving this reference to it. Fixed.

-There were some obvious grammar errors in the Tutorial that I thought were fixed for the last update but they were not (which I am a little confused about). In any case, I have gone through the Tutorial and fixed everything I found, though there may still be small imperfections (New Tutorial coming soon so I'm only worrying about the big mistakes).

-In certain circumstances there may have been a crash when clicking on an unusable upgrade button. This is fixed.

-The Game may have been Pausing automatically when placing your Headquarters- it does not do this anymore.

-When upgrading sometimes the selected tower/wall/mine would deselect. This should no longer happen

-Added preview to Out of Game Options for the Transparency Level. You could adjust it before through the Menu but since it only applies to in-game HUD backgrounds there was no way to see a preview before.

-There have also been a lot of other general small fixes/tweaks.

notes.title: Progress Report 4
notes.notes:
Hey folks, the Release has been a bit overwhelming, but not too much so- I’m pretty satisfied with how things are going- I really needed some feedback, I got some, and now the Game is improving. My best work has been collaborative projects and I really want to know what you think needs work, or balanced differently so please let me know. That’s the one thing I can’t get too much of- feedback!


What’s been going on since Release?

I'm excited to have released the first decent Patch a few days ago which fix a lot of small things and greatly improve the HUD. I’ve been compiling a list based on your feedback and addressing it. There are still things to do, the primary focus is general improvements based on your feedback right now. The HUD was pretty bland before, and the HUD background was too transparent- transparency is adjustable now. the HUD took up too much space, some buttons didn’t match the style of the Game, there were a few bugs and some grammar mistakes, most of which are taken care of. I’m still working on the HUD, but it’s getting pretty close to something I’m okay with. The Game should be very stable with this newest Patch. I haven’t found much wrong with the Gameplay for a few days (I try to get a Game or two in every day).


Leaderboard System

This is the next feature I want to add to the Game, which I’m just getting started on. I’m hoping to release this with the Tutorial replacement, a couple weeks down the road, but we’ll see how that goes. The first version will be Local only, you will be able to compare with anyone who plays on your installation, then an online version so you can compare scores with anyone who plays.


Achievements

To be honest, I was so consumed with finishing the Game that I totally overlooked achievements. Thanks to feedback I was reminded and I think it’s important for a Game like this. It is something that shouldn’t be too hard to add, but it’ll take some time. I’ve got a running list of achievements that will be added once I get to this, if you have any suggestions, don’t hesitate to mention it. Achievements are a pretty high priority, though first I want to get the HUD finished, generally polish and balance what is here already and add in a Local Leaderboard system. 


The Tutorial

I was very unhappy with how the Tutorial turned out (why I never made that video about it), and I’ve gotten some good feedback about how to make it better. I’ve made some minor fixes to the current Tutorial, though I’m not putting too much effort into it since I’m totally replacing it with a tips style Tutorial. No slide shows, no locked navigation, no forcing the player to Build their base a certain way; at the time of this writing the current Tutorial does this and force feeds you way too much information all at once. It just isn’t done well.

The initial part of the new Tutorial guides you on where to place your Headquarters without limiting you. You can still Build wherever you want. Then it suggests how to use your initial 8 Population. After that it becomes adaptive, it keeps an eye out for imbalances in your Base and helps you to know what to Build as you progress, also telling you why it is making the suggestion. It will let you know when Available Population is at 0 or negative, showing you where to buy a House. If you are losing Food or Food is at 0 it will show you where to get a Farm. If you haven’t upgraded anything by a certain Wave it will make sure you know about upgrades, if you haven’t expanded your Build area it will tell you about Supply Depots, which expand where you can Build. That’s just a few of the things it watches for, there are more. This way you can go straight into playing on any Map without playing through a dedicated Tutorial first, you can use it until the Game makes sense and turn it off any time, in or out of Game, or you can turn it on in the middle of the Game if you feel you are missing something. I’m about half way done with it, it’ll be a couple weeks before it’s finished, this is something I revisit ever few days when I need a challenge- the adaptive part is tricky but I think it’s a pretty neat system!


So anyway, that’s it for this Report. Things are coming along at a steady pace. I’m excited to get moving and get this Game finished! I hope this first patch shows that your opinions matter! Expect another Report in about 2 Weeks, I’m hoping to have another Patch out before then. Anyway, take care folks!

notes.title: Mini-Patch 2 v 0.04.39
notes.notes:
I realized that the Game Over section of the screen turns White- I had to add a bit of code to the HUD to make the transparency adjustable and missed the Game Over background. This is fixed now.

I thought it was important that Players be able to read the Game Over screen. I guess I need to let the Games I play finish more often! That's how I caught it- I admit, I do play a lot myself. Thanks for your support folks! I'll be releasing another Progress Report soon.

notes.title: Grid Creeps Patch 1
notes.notes:
It's been a week, and I have been busy. I have the first regular patch, which addresses many issues. A lot of improvements have been made and bugs addressed. I've gotten some good feedback and hope that this Update reflects that. I haven't addressed everything I want to based on the feedback I've gotten, but I hope you'll agree, there are some big improvements! Read the change log below to see the biggest changes this week-


-Major HUD changes. Compare the first and second screenshot to see the update.

-HUD Buttons have been Updated to match the style of the Game. The Buttons should be easier to read and just plain look better.

-The HUD background Opacity was too transparent, making it hard to read text sometimes. An Option has been added that allows you to choose your own level of transparency any time.

-The 'Wave:', 'Gold:' and Gold 'Income' Information Text (Largest Text) has been made smaller and the HUD background behind these things has been shifted to account for the smaller size, giving the Player more screenspace.

-The Tower Target Priority buttons were very large, also taking up a lot of screen-space. They are much smaller, giving you a better view of the Level when a Tower is selected.

-Options settings were not loading as intended in many situations, giving the appearance that it wasn't remembering your settings between games and Options were acting strange in general. It was referencing the wrong file type when checking to see if a certain file existed when re-starting the Game, loading a Level and starting a new Game. Now in all these cases, the Game will remember the Options settings and should operate as expected. 

-Added preview to the Farm Land Build Area and added a Build effect to the Farm Land. This should fix a few different small problems with Building Farms and assist in planning your Base. It also disallows building on future Farm land that is in the Build Process.

-Converting the Archer Tower to the Ballista Tower causes the Tower to be Destroyed. This was a minor code flaw and has been fixed, you can convert an Archer into a Ballista without any problems now.

-The Tutorial has been Edited to help better explain itself and the Game. (I am currently working on a much better Tutorial to replace this one)

-After level 20 the last few creeps per Wave will catch on fire. This is to temporarily address a small problem with the AI finding the HQ in certain circumstances during the late Game. In the future I will be doing some work on the AI which will address this and make it a little bit smarter.

-When selecting the Blaster or Laser Towers they both had the wrong label, although the other information about each Tower was correct. This has been fixed.

-Disabled the ability to Save on the empty Loading Level. (Game would crash when loading a Save performed here)

-When exiting from the Main screen, if you clicked on the 'Exit Game' Button more than once it would create multiple Yes/No Buttons. No more!


-In the Archer Description when Selected it said the Archer can miss, this is an error that has been fixed- the Archer, Fire Archer and Crossbow never miss, though the Ballista can.

-Many other minor bugs/improvements have been made as well.


That's all for this first Week. I expect to release the next patch sometime within the next Week or Two, so let me know what changes you want to see!

notes.title: Mini-Patch 1 (v.0.03.37)
notes.notes:
This bug was reported earlier today by a Player.

-If a Tower, Mine, or Wall that was Selected got Destroyed the Upgrade/Target Priority Buttons wouldn't disappear. The code used the selected object's ID (an arbitrary number assigned by the game) but since it didn't exist anymore due to it having been destroyed the Game got mad and rage-quit. Now the buttons know they are suppose to go away when the tower does so the Game will remain happy and won't rage-quit on you anymore.

If you find a bug that causes the game to crash then a grey box will pop up, gives an error and bits of code. If you can get the information to me through a screenshot or copy/pasting I will try to fix it immediately. 

-There is a known issue when alt-tabbing. you will get an error box like the game is crashing but there will be an option to ignore- do just that, it doesn't cause any problems. This minor bug has to do with the buildable area showing when alt-tabbing/minimizing, the code is kept in temporary memory which is wiped when alt-tabbing/minimizing but as soon as you ignore it the game continues like nothing happened. This will be fixed soon.

notes.title: Grid Creeps Released!
notes.notes:
Grid Creeps has been Released! Build up your Base and Defend your Headquarters from ever more numerous and powerful Creeps!

The next 3 to 6 Months will be spent putting together an Online Leaderboard so that Players can compare how far they got with each other. An Editor is in the works so that you can craft your own Levels. Support for more OS/Devices is also on the Horizon.

There are other smaller additions and improvements to come. First and foremost, with the first patch within a week or two a Local Leaderboard will be added to keep track of the furthest you have gotten on each Level, but this version will only compare to people who play on the system that has the game installed on it- the online Leaderboard is quite a bit more work, but it is at the top of my to-do list once the basic Local version is completed.

Expect more Levels, a wider variety of music, more Creep types, including a Boss Creep that will show up every now and then to demolish your defenses! I would also like to add Randomization for Resource Distribution on each level giving each Level near limitless possibilities.

Support for MacOS/Ubuntu is coming as well with 1.0 and after that testing on tablets/phones/web browser is planned.

And of course there are a lot of smaller additions/improvements I'd like to make but there's time for that in future Announcements

There are big plans for this project, I'm excited to be its author! And if you've read all that I've posted, then this last part will sound a bit repetitive- I hope you all enjoy the Game and have a wonderful day!

And please- let me know if you have any suggestions! Feedback is important!

notes.title: Progress Report 3
notes.notes:
Hey folks, I'm going to keep this one short for the same reason I'm a bit late on this last update before Release- it's crunch time and I need to devote as much time to finalizing the Game as possible, hopefully my grammar isn't too bad. There was a short time that I was afraid I might have to post-pone the release for a few days so I could finalize some things, but I got lucky and the things that I thought were going to push off the release date fell into place. So here's the quick and dirty of it.


[h1]Targeting Priority[/h1]

The system is totally finished and implemented. This was a feature I didn't think would make it into Early Access, so this is a great bonus! 

You can prioritize by: 

1. Target Highest Hitpoints 
2. Target Lowest Hitpoints 
3. Target Closest to Me (tower that is being assigned)
4. Target Furthest from me (tower that is being assigned)
5. Target Closest to Headquarters 
6. Target Furthest from Headquarters, 
7. Target Red Creeps first
8. Target Blue Creeps first
9. Target Green Creeps first
10. Target Yellow Creeps first


[h1]The Tutorial[/h1]

I am still tweaking the tutorial to make it a little easier to understand. I was going to release a trailer showing it off but I just don't have the time to get that done- I'm keeping this update quick so that I can get back to working on the Game. However, in place of the Tutorial trailer, in the last 3-4 days before release I have to get the version of the Game that will be released approved by Steam, so I will have some 'freetime' just before launch; I will be making a new, much better trailer, which includes a preview of the menus, should include a preview of the Game music and will replace all screenshots with updated ones- the HUD layout is the same but the style has been greatly improved, which will be shown in the video/screenshots.


[h1]Tool Tips[/h1]

In addition to the Tutorial I will be adding in a 'Tool Tips' Option which can be enabled and will work in any Game you play if enabled in the Options. 'Tool Tips' are seperate from the Tutorial but serve the same purpose in guiding the player with pointers as you play to help you know when you might need to build a certain structure, or if you are losing Resources before it's too late and should help those who are new to the game in managing their base and Creep Defense without as much guess work. Unfortunately there is a the chances are low that this will be included in the initial release, however I do plan to release a patch within the first week of release that adds this feature.


[h1]About Music and Sound Effects-[/h1]

This is my main focus until release. The Game itself is pretty much ready for release besides the audio end. I am on a hunt for the right music. I am also replacing/improving some of the effects and there are some objects which are missing their Sounds (Lightning Tower, Rail Gun, etc.)


[h1]High Score Tracking-[/h1]

I am doing my best to get the more important aspects ready for release right now. I would like for there to at least be a localized high score system for each level so that players can try to beat their old scores. I am not sure that this I will be able to add this before the first release. If it is not in the first release I will be releasing an update within the first week or two which adds this in. Eventually, as noted in other updates, the ultimate goal is to have a World Leaderboard which allows people all over the World to compete for the top 10 high score for the day/week and maybe month, but this is a lot more work than a localized version which requires me to learn new skills unrelated to the toolsets I have used to make the game. So anyway, to sum it up- if local high scores are not in the initial release, they will be added for the first patch, which should be a week or two after initial release.


[h1]What's next?[/h1]

There is still some balancing to do, which I may not be totally happy with by release, though since I have made the game and know all it's secrets I am bias, which makes balancing difficult. I will continue balancing and improvements after Release and I want to know what you think needs nerfing/boosting, I want to know how you think the Game can be improved because there will be many patches before the Official 1.0 release


[h1]On a personal note[/h1]

This is the last update before Releasing the Game! I'll be honest- I am very excited, and equally nervousness about this release. I have been parts of teams that have released games, one was a large scale project with hundreds of people, but never on my own. I've put a whole lot of time into this and I hope it gives you many hours of entertainment and challenge! 

I apologize if this update isn't as well thought out as my previous updates, these normally take a couple of days to get right but I just winged it this time around- I need to get back to working on the Game itself so it can be as good as possible; crunch-mode is in effect! 

Lastly, I hope you're all having a great day!

notes.title: Progress Report 2
notes.notes:
Time for the next update! I meant to get this out a couple of days ago but I had an unexpected side job helping convert a Bathtub into a walk in shower for a family member with failing Health- remodeling has been my profession for the past decade, a passionless endeavor that doesn’t challenge my brain in a rewarding way; I hope to replace this with Game Design, with this Game being my first foray after a decade of Game Development as a hobby. The job has delayed the progress report a bit but it is complete and I have been hard at work catching up to get this out ASAP. Despite the unexpected Job I have made more progress than expected on the Game itself. See below!


[h1]HUD Background[/h1]

The HUD background has been updated. The new background makes it easier to see the Game behind the the HUD while also serving its purpose of making it easier to read text. I hope you will also agree that it matches the style of the rest of the HUD elements and just plain looks a lot better. The first screenshot shows the updated HUD elements while all the others show the old HUD. 


[h1]Grid Creeps Guide[/h1]

Version 1 is complete! With this Update it is available for you to check out. It explains the mechanics of the Game and shows all of the important stats. The values are subject to changes as the game is balanced; things such as Range, Hitpoints, Damage or a number of other values will likely change as the game matures but the Mechanics behind those numbers are set in stone and should be helpful in understanding how the Game works. It explains the differences between the 16 Towers and what makes them unique, it talks about what every building’s purpose is and hopefully gives a general idea of how all the different aspects of the Game are woven together. The Guide should speak for itself, the Download can be found along the right side where the website link is located. If you have any questions or something isn’t explained clearly, please let me know. I hope this helps you to understand what I hope you’ll be playing in less than a Month if this sort of Game is your cup of tea.

[h1][url=http://gridcreeps.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Grid-Creeps-Guide.pdf]Grid Creeps Game Guide can be found here[/url][/h1]

[h1]Tower Target Priority[/h1]

I was skeptical that this would make it into the initial Early Access version of the Game, but somehow I managed to finish the code side of things in just a few days. It is not implemented yet, but is confirmed working as intended. I still need to make the Buttons and code the bits for switching between priorities- the interactive part of the system, which is easy work, if not a bit monotonous. I am hoping the next update will see this part of the Game finished and this is the reason that I have decided not to follow through with the Tutorial Trailer this week, but more on that below.


[h1]The Tutorial[/h1]

I was planning on releasing a video of the Tutorial this week, but with the addition of the Target Priority system the Tutorial cannot be completed until that part of the Tutorial is added- they are bound together at this point. I did not expect the Priority System to be complete so quickly! What I thought would take weeks took about 3 Days (Love it when that happens!). Now that it will be complete in time for Release things have changed a bit and I can’t deliver on the Tutorial Trailer until I get the Priority system done, this is what I am working on as soon as this Update is completed. I see no reason why I won’t be able to get these things done in the next two Weeks, but you never know with life- I wasn’t expecting to be converting a bathroom last week which delayed things a bit, but it is something I had to do for someone who is important to me and my Family. The Tutorial will be more complete and it gives me some extra time to polish what is already finished.


[h1]About Music[/h1]

As you may have noticed there is no Music in the trailer. That is because there is none yet, but I have been doing my homework and hunting down a good match for the Game. Ideally I would make the Music myself, but I no longer have the Software I used to use to make Music and it is expensive. I hope to have made a decision on how to handle Music by the next Progress Report, but I can’t guarantee that I will have gotten to that yet. Despite the next Bi-Weekly Progress Report being the last before Release, if there is no Music decision yet I will make an extra Report before release at some point to show off the Music that will come with the Game. There will always be an option to turn it off if you don’t like it, so no worries- it is not forced upon you. Anyway, that is the plan for Music.


[h1]What’s next?[/h1]

The next pre-release Progress Report will be the last one before the Game is released (unless Music has not been decided by then). By then I hope that all the information you might need in order to make a decision on whether or not to purchase the Game will be available. The only things left are to fully implement the Target Priority System, finish the Tutorial and ruthlessly hunt out and destroy any bugs in the Game along with a bit of Polish to Art if time permits. Eventually, post-Early Access Release, I hope to start animating some parts of the Game Art to breath more life into the Game.

I am always in the Group Chat and my email is gridcreeps@gridcreeps.com, so if you have any questions or suggestions you are free to contact me any time. Thank you for your interest in Grid Creeps and have a Wonderful Day!

notes.title: Progress Report 1
notes.notes:
Alright folks, time for the first update! It’s been a busy past 2 weeks since the Announcement, so let’s get to it!...


[h1]The Tutorial-[/h1]

This has been the primary focus of the last 2 weeks. On announcing Grid Creeps the Tutorial was just a slide show with a lot of text, but it has now been replaced with an interactive walkthrough that has much less to read. The new Tutorial guides the player through first explaining the information presented on the HUD before walking the Player through the process of building a simple Base without the hassle of an impending attack. When the Tutorial is over the Player gains full Control of the Game and you can play it out as you normally would. Naturally, Tutorial Mode is set on Easy. This part of the Game has been a Challenge, but it is almost complete!


[h1]Grid Creeps Guide-[/h1]

This next Update will focus on explaining the Game’s details, which will include a video of the Tutorial and this Guide. The Guide will explain the Game’s mechanics in detail and should answer most questions you may have about how the Game works.


[h1]Tower Target Priority-[/h1]

This is the next thing I will be working on after the Tutorial is finished. There are some minor imperfections with the current system, which is fully automated at the moment- Towers shoot at the closest Enemy they can see. The new system will give the Player options, allowing the Player to choose how each Tower picks its targets, like shoot at the Strongest, Weakest, Closest to the Headquarters, certain color Creeps, etc. 


[h1]The Leaderboard-[/h1]

I have started preliminary work on an Online Leaderboard, though for the time being there are more pressing issues that need attention before I dive deeper into it. I view this as my biggest challenge, which I don’t expect to be ready on the first Early Access Release. Online Leaderboards are a step up in difficulty for me compared to making the local Leaderboard and the Game itself; it’s something I haven’t done before but this Game wouldn’t exist if I hadn’t done a whole load of things I’d never done before. I also have some technical decisions to make on how best to implement it.

There will also be a local Leaderboard which only counts the Games that you have played, so that you can play against yourself and anyone else who plays on your Machine while the Online version is being worked on. If this isn’t in the very first Early Access Release then it will be in the first Patch- I am optimistic, though I don’t want to over-promise. 


[h1]What’s new with the Creeps?[/h1]

Blue Creep is the fellow that has seen changes. This week I have added in what makes this enemy unique- when he dies 4 Baby Blue Creeps are born. With their small size, they can fit between some Buildings and Towers without having to destroy them first to get to your Headquarters. Some Towers might also have trouble hitting them thanks to their small size. You won’t see these little guys in the First Trailer since they’re new. I still need to tweak the code slightly to keep these little fellows from occasionally getting stuck in things you’ve built, otherwise Blue Creep is just about ready for Release.

Regarding the other Creeps, they’re ready for Release- Red is your Standard Baddie, with mediocre stats. Green is the Sniper of the bunch, with longer Range and a more powerful attack but Green Creep is the slowest and has lower Hit Points than the others. Yellow Creep Explodes when he dies and is the fastest of them all, but his regular attack is the weak with the lowest Range. Expect more detailed information when the Game Guide that is mentioned above is Released.


[h1]What’s next?[/h1]

Expect these Progress Reports about every two weeks. The next update will contain a lot of information about the Game with a video of the Tutorial and the Game Guide along with a general update about what I’ve been working on. Thank you for checking out Grid Creeps! 


I am always in the Group Chat, so if you have any questions you are free to check in there any time.
